1→# Personal CV and Resume
     2→
     3→This repository contains my personal Curriculum Vitae (CV) and Résumé, built using a modified version of the "Awesome CV" LaTeX template. Both documents are structured to align with the recommendations of the Finnish National Board on Research Integrity TENK 2020 template for researchers.
     4→
     5→## Documents
     6→
     7→*   **`cv.tex`**: My comprehensive Curriculum Vitae, following the TENK guidelines.
     8→*   **`resume.tex`**: My concise Résumé, also structured according to TENK recommendations. This document utilizes a modular approach, drawing content from individual `.tex` files within the `resume/` directory.
     9→*   **`coverletter.tex`**: A LaTeX template for a cover letter.
    10→
    11→## How to Use
    12→
    13→To compile these documents, you will need a full TeX distribution installed on your system (e.g., TeX Live).
    14→
    15→Navigate to the root directory of this repository in your terminal and execute the following commands to generate the PDF files:
    16→
    17→*   **To compile the CV:**
    18→    ```bash
    19→    xelatex cv.tex
    20→    ```
    21→
    22→*   **To compile the Résumé:**
    23→    ```bash
    24→    xelatex resume.tex
    25→    ```
    26→
    27→*   **To compile the Cover Letter:**
    28→    ```bash
    29→    xelatex coverletter.tex
    30→    ```
    31→
    32→Each command will generate a corresponding PDF file (e.g., `cv.pdf`, `resume.pdf`, `coverletter.pdf`) in the same directory.
    33→
    34→## Structure
    35→
    36→The project structure is organized as follows:
    37→
    38→*   `awesome-cv.cls`: The core LaTeX class file for the template.
    39→*   `cv.tex`: Main CV document.
    40→*   `resume.tex`: Main Résumé document, which includes sections from the `resume/` directory.

1→# CLAUDE.md
     2→
     3→This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
     4→
     5→## Project Overview
     6→
     7→LaTeX-based CV/Resume project using the **Awesome CV** template, structured to comply with the TENK 2020 (Finnish National Board on Research Integrity) guidelines for academic researchers.
     8→
     9→## Build Commands
    10→
    11→Requires a full TeX distribution (e.g., TeX Live) with **XeLaTeX** (needed for TTF font support and Unicode):
    12→
    13→```bash
    14→xelatex cv.tex           # Compile the full CV
    15→xelatex resume.tex       # Compile the résumé
    16→xelatex coverletter.tex  # Compile the cover letter
    17→```
    18→
    19→Each produces a corresponding PDF in the project root.
    20→
    21→## Architecture
    22→
    23→- **`awesome-cv.cls`** — Core LaTeX class file defining all styling, custom commands, and layout. This is the template engine shared by all documents.
    24→- **`cv.tex`** — Monolithic CV document; all content is inline in one file.
    25→- **`resume.tex`** — Modular résumé; includes section files from `resume/` via `\input{}`.
    26→- **`coverletter.tex`** — Cover letter template.
    27→- **`resume/`** — Individual `.tex` section files (degrees, experience, awards, etc.). Several are placeholders (funding, supervision, teaching, merits, impact) marked with TODO comments.
    28→- **`cv/`** — Section files for the CV (education, experience, honors, skills, etc.), though `cv.tex` currently embeds its content directly.
    29→- **`fonts/`** — Roboto font family (11 variants) and FontAwesome TTF, loaded by `awesome-cv.cls` via `fontspec`.
    30→
    31→## Key Conventions
    32→
    33→- Color theme is set per document (e.g., `\colorlet{awesome}{awesome-skyblue}` in cv.tex, `awesome-red` in coverletter.tex).
    34→- Personal info is configured via commands like `\name`, `\position`, `\email`, `\github`, `\linkedin` in each main `.tex` file's preamble.
    35→- The resume uses `\input{resume/<section>.tex}` for modularity — add new sections by creating a file in `resume/` and adding the corresponding `\input` in `resume.tex`.
    36→- The `orcidlink` package is used in `cv.tex` for ORCID integration.
    37→

     4→
     5→## Project Overview
     6→
     7→This repository contains the static website for the **HydroImaging** workshop — "Mining Imaging Data for Hydrological and Environmental Modelling" — hosted at IEEE ICIP 2026, Tampere, Finland.
     8→
     9→The website is deployed via GitHub Pages from: `https://github.com/midhem-icip2026/midhem-icip2026.github.io`
    10→
    11→Local working directory: `/scratch/gdemil24/ICIP2026/hydroimaging.github.io/`
    12→
    13→## Repository Structure
    14→
    15→```
    16→hydroimaging.github.io/
    17→  index.html          # Entire website — single self-contained HTML file
    18→  assets/             # Images and video used by the site
    19→    *.jpg / *.png     # Speaker photos, hero background, visualizations
    20→    hero-video.mp4    # Hero section background video
    21→    tampere/          # Additional Tampere imagery
    22→```
    23→
    24→## Development Workflow
    25→
    26→There is no build step. The site is a single `index.html` with all CSS and JavaScript inline. To preview, open `index.html` directly in a browser or serve it locally:
    27→
    28→```bash
    29→python3 -m http.server 8080
    30→# then open http://localhost:8080
    31→```
    32→
    33→To deploy, commit and push to `main` on the GitHub remote — GitHub Pages auto-publishes:
    34→
    35→```bash
    36→git add index.html assets/
    37→git commit -m "..."
    38→git push origin main
    39→```
    40→
    41→## Architecture of index.html (1808 lines)
    42→
    43→The file is structured in this order:
    44→1. **`<head>`** — fonts (Google Fonts: Inter, Space Grotesk, JetBrains Mono), Font Awesome CDN, all inline CSS
    45→2. **CSS** (~830 lines) — CSS custom properties for dark/light themes, component styles (navbar, glass cards, badges, buttons, waves, responsive grid)
    46→3. **HTML sections** (in DOM order):
    47→   - `#navbar` — fixed nav with dark/light toggle and mobile hamburger
    48→   - `#hero` — full-screen hero with background video/image and tagline
    49→   - `#about` — workshop description and ICIP 2026 info banner
    50→   - `#speakers` — invited speakers grid with photo cards
    51→   - `#schedule` — workshop program table (placeholder until schedule confirmed)
    52→   - `#cfp` — call for papers with topics, submission guidelines
    53→   - `#dates` — key deadlines table
    54→   - `#organizers` — organizer cards (senior + early-career)
    55→   - `#sponsors` — sponsor logos/info
    56→   - `<footer>` — links and copyright
    57→4. **JavaScript** (~100 lines at end) — IntersectionObserver for fade-in animations, navbar scroll behavior, mobile menu toggle, dark/light theme toggle
    58→
    59→## Theming
    60→
    61→Two themes are implemented via CSS custom properties on `<html data-theme="...">`:
    62→- Dark (default): deep navy/blue palette
    63→- Light: light blue/white palette
    64→
    65→The toggle is in the navbar JS at the bottom of the file.
